classification_contract.operative_tool_call: An instruction in execution steps explicitly telling an agent to call the Skill tool, including calls inside delegated subagent instructions.
classification_contract.operative_slash_call: An imperative to use a named skill in execution steps without explicit Skill-tool wording. Still a dependency, not router prose.
classification_contract.human_only_prerequisite: Tell a human to invoke a user-only skill, or require input/config generated by one. Never satisfy by calling that user-only skill from another skill.
classification_contract.soft_document_pointer: Read glossary/ADRs/standards if present, without actively changing the domain model. Not an edge to domain-modeling.
classification_contract.plain_router_suggestion: Human-facing labels, future suggested skills, examples and workflow narration. Not current agent dispatch.
classification_contract.owned_resource: Reference/template/script/credit file co-located in the owning skill. Must travel with its full directory.
classification_contract.dynamic_call: Runtime skill names provided by user-authored map Notes. Validate model invocation and exact provider before dispatch.
classification_contract.runtime_capability: Subagents, browser/file opener, authenticated tracker CLI, git worktrees, test runner or web reading. These are capabilities, not inferred named-agent files.
classification_contract.credit_only: Attribution to copied material. No named-skill runtime dependency.

Current bodies additionally require tracker setup for code-review and implement-spec; wayfinder has both a setup pointer and local fallback. Bodies take precedence over this historical example list.

additional_importer_blockers.evidence: tree_digest excludes PROVENANCE.md and .vendor-owned.json only; process_source compares root support tree to upstream, then writes LICENSE.upstream and ATTRIBUTION.md into that same root. The next check sees extra generated legal files and reports perpetual drift.
additional_importer_blockers.decision: Parent must make importer-generated root metadata invisible to source-content comparison without masking real upstream resources. Scope exclusions by ownership and root location, not broad filename exemptions. Add no-drift repeated-sync test.

additional_importer_blockers.evidence: clone_source uses git clone --depth 1 --branch source.ref, and records checkout sha separately. pinned_commit is a historical comparison value, not an enforced checkout pin.
additional_importer_blockers.decision: Use locally verified tag v1.3.1 for this release and check cloned HEAD equals 24fe0ef7737efae15c87225755e9f6f5965e4888 before applying. Raw SHA is not accepted by git clone --branch. A future release needs intentional ref update, rather than assuming setting pinned_commit freezes main.

ambiguities_and_limits: This is static source/configuration analysis, not proof of harness tool availability or installed skill resolution.
No external services were queried or written, no upstream installers/scripts/instructions were executed, and neither repository was edited.
Current inventory pin does not describe the 24 live Matt-style bodies. Historical exact-match evidence distinguishes older upstream snapshots from local adaptations.
caveman/write-a-skill provenance claims are not anchored to their actual originating upstream commits by the existing inventory.
Human alias implementation is harness-dependent and absent today.
The existing research duplicate can remain lint-baselined at current paths without new debt, but name-only runtime dispatch is still ambiguous.
Explicit path dispatch is only valid if the actual harness supports and verifies it; do not infer it from local directory names.

Current sync_vendor.py has no built-in archive/adoption mode. Proposed per-skill support entries need an explicit parent migration design; normal first sync against populated native trees fails closed.
PR credits establish attribution and deny a runtime dependency. This audit does not independently verify licensing of Humanlayer copied material.
Wayfinder Notes and handoff suggested skills are open-ended, not statically enumerable named dependencies.
TDD requires human-confirmed seams while implement-spec encourages AFK concurrency. Pass the previously agreed seams from spec/ticket context; do not have workers invent confirmation.

Concurrent implement-spec merger agents need serialized integration-branch updates and revalidation if the tip moves. Merging a tip before reporting does not mathematically guarantee fast-forward when another worker merges meanwhile.
Imported architecture-report template loads Tailwind and Mermaid from CDNs; the source bundle is local but that output is not offline-self-contained.
Local doc says gh 2.4.0; this audit records the policy text, not a verified current binary.
Upstream no longer has resolving-merge-conflicts. Archiving rather than silently wiping it preserves local history without asserting an upstream replacement.

Per-skill support mapping with to empty string shares its mapping root with generated license/attribution. Existing digest does not ignore those two generated root files, so repeated support-root sync reports false drift until importer comparison is corrected and tested.

The locally available v1.3.1 tag points at the audited commit. Current clone_source uses ref rather than pinned_commit to select content; require SHA equality before first import and intentional future ref updates.
